params.body:
A gateway carries the configuration it was given until an operator carries over a new one, and nothing told the hands which version that was. On 14 September a new project (`vera`) sat in the configuration on the box while the VM still served the grant from before it, and the only sign was a hand refused with `resource not in grant`: correct, and unreadable — the refusal names the resource, not the staleness.

`GET /v1/agents` now carries `grants`, one entry per agent with a digest of its `kinds` and its `resources`: sorted, newline-joined, sha-256. Anyone holding the same list computes the same value, so a difference is a real difference and never a reshuffle, and the lists themselves stay out of the answer.

With this, Elixir's supervisor can compare the configuration it writes with what the VM serves and say "carry it over" in its job note, instead of a hand finding out an hour later.

Reading stays open, as it is for records and attachments: evidence is for strangers.
params.title: Agents say what they may touch, as a digest
